div.head: II As 3
div.ab: Be ryhtes wærnunge. Se hlaford se ryhtes wyrne ond for his yfelan mon licge: ⁊ mon ðone cing foresece, forgilde þæt ceapgild ⁊ gesylle þam cynge CXX scll'. ⁊ se ðe ðone cyng sece, ær he him ryhtes bidde swa oft swa him togebyrie, gilde ðæt ilce wite þe se oþer sceolde, gif he him ryhtes wyrnde.

And se hlaford ðe rihtes wyrne and for his yfelan man licge: ⁊ man ðone cyng forséce, forgylde þæt ceapgyld ⁊ gesylle ðam cynge hundtwelftig scill'. ⁊ se ðe ðæne cyng séce, ær he hine rihtes bidde swa oft swa him togebyrige, gylde þæt ilce wite þæt se oðer sceolde, gyf he him rihtes wyrnde.

And se hlaford ryhtes wyrne ⁊ for his yfelan men lycge: ⁊ mon þonne cyning forsece, forgylde þæt ceapgyld ⁊ gesylle þam cyning CXX scill'. And se þe þonne cyning sece, ær he him ryhtes bidde swa oft swa him togebyrige, gyld þæt ylce wite þe se oðer sceold, gif he him ryhtes forwyrnd.

Et dominus, qui rectum difforciabit et malum hominem suum manutenebit, ut regem oporteat inde requiri, captale suum repetenti restituat et emendet regi CXX sol. Et qui regem requisierit, antequam sibi rectum roget quociens pertinet ad hoc, emendet ipsam wytam (id est forisfacturam), quam alius emendare debuerat, si rectum (iusticiam) difforciasset.

Be ryhtes wærnunge. Se hlaford se ryhtes wyrne ond for his yfelan mon licge: ⁊ mon ðone cing foresece, forgilde þæt ceapgild ⁊ gesylle þam cynge CXX scll'. ⁊ se ðe ðone cyng sece ær he him ryhtes bidde swa oft swa him togebyrie, gilde ðæt ilce wite þe se oþer sceolde, gif he him ryhtes wyrnde.

Über Rechtsverweigerung. Der Herr, welcher [einem Kläger] den Rechtsgang weigert, indem er für seinen schuldigen Untergebenen sich einsetzt: [wenn] man [Kläger] den König (nun So) angeht [um Rechtsschutz], so bezahle [der Herr dem Kläger] den Sachwerth und gebe dem König 120 Schill. Wer dagegen den König angeht, bevor er sich, so oft wie ihm zukommt, Recht [daheim] erbittet, bezahle dasselbe Strafgeld, welches der Gegner schulden würde, wenn dieser ihm Rechtsgang geweigert hätte.

On refusal of justice. The lord who refuses [a plaintiff] legal process by standing up for his guilty dependant: [if] one [the plaintiff] (then, So) applies to the king [for redress], let [the lord] pay [the plaintiff] the value of the goods and give the king 120 shillings. But whoever applies to the king before he has asked for justice [at home] as often as is due to him, let him pay the same fine that the opponent would owe if he had refused him legal process.

If a lord refuses justice, by taking the part of one of his men who has done wrong, and application is made to the king [about the matter, the lord] shall pay the value of the goods [in dispute] and give 120 shillings to the king. He who applies to the king before he pleads as often as is required for justice [at home], shall pay the same fine as the other would have had [to pay] if he had refused him [the plaintiff] justice.

Concerning the refusal of justice. The lord who refuses justice and upholds his guilty man, so that the king is appealed to, is to repay the value of the goods and 120 shillings to the king; and he who appeals to the king before he demands justice as often as he ought, is to pay the same fine as the other would have done, if he had refused him justice.

Nicht Justizweigerung (s. d. Gl) durch private Gerichtsbarkeit (s. d. Gl 26 g. 33 a) liegt hier vor, wie Cohn Justizverweigerung 113 meint. Sondern dieser Herr begeht nur Rechtsweigerung (s. d. Gl 5. a), indem er den Untergebenen vors staatliche Lokalgericht zu stellen oder statt seiner dort Ersatz, Busse und Strafe zu zahlen unterlässt (so Maitland Domesday 284; Maurer Kr. Übsch. II 31), so dass der Zweck des Zwanges unter Vassallität in 2 verfehlt wird. Und der lokale Vogt ist zu ohnmächtig, den Herrn zu zwingen. Solche übermächtige Rechtsweigerer muss IV As 3 verpflanzen (s. d. Gl) oder VI 8, 2 f. bekämpfen durch Aufgebot mehrerer Nachbarvögte. In Schottland traten noch im 18. Jh. Clans der Justiz entgegen; Pol Mai I 17. 27. — Es scheint nur Eine lokale Gerichtsinstanz unterhalb des Königsgerichts (s. d. Gl 3. a) gemeint, nicht, wie später, über dem Hundred die Grafschaft zu stehen. Vgl. Gl Instanzenzug 5. a. b

What we have here is not denial of justice (see that word in Gl) by a private jurisdiction (see that word in Gl 26 g. 33 a), as Cohn Justizverweigerung 113 thinks. Rather, this lord commits only refusal of right (see that word in Gl 5. a), in that he fails to produce his subordinate before the state's local court, or to pay restitution, compensation and fine there in his stead (so Maitland Domesday 284; Maurer Kr. Übsch. II 31), so that the purpose of the compulsion through vassalage in 2 is defeated. And the local reeve is too powerless to compel the lord. Such over-mighty refusers of right IV As 3 has to transplant (see that word in Gl), and VI 8, 2 f. to combat by calling out several neighbouring reeves. In Scotland clans still opposed justice in the 18th cent.; Pol Mai I 17. 27. — Only one local court instance below the king's court (see that word in Gl 3. a) seems to be meant, not, as later, the shire standing above the hundred. Cf. Gl Instanzenzug 5. a. b
Nicht ‘des Untergebenen Sache zur eigenen macht’, wie Toller 637 a versteht; vielmehr ‘schützend vertritt’
Not ‘makes the subordinate's cause his own’, as Toller 637 a understands it; rather ‘represents him protectively’
Vielleicht steht auch in hb þone statt þonne (s. d. Wb 223 Sp. 2 Z. 6 v. u.); ‘König’ ohne Artikel wäre gut archaisch
Perhaps hb too has þone instead of þonne (see that word in Wb 223 col. 2 l. 6 from the bottom); ‘king’ without the article would be good archaic usage
Schmid nimmt fore gegen Thorpe als Adverb
Schmid, against Thorpe, takes fore as an adverb
‘Des Gestohlenen, laut 3, 1, oder allgemein Prozessobjekt’; Cohn 114
‘Of the stolen goods, according to 3, 1, or in general the object of the suit’; Cohn 114
Ungehorsam; s. d. Gl 23; falsche Klage 7 b. c
Disobedience; see that word in Gl 23; falsche Klage 7 b. c
Nach Landrecht oder Ortsbrauch, später dreimal; nicht, wie Cohn meint, wechselnd nach Person des Klägers oder Richters
According to the law of the land or local custom, later three times; not, as Cohn thinks, varying according to the person of the plaintiff or judge
Auch der Beschwerde über Justizweigerung bei Franken und Burgundern muss, nach Cohn, mehrmalige Rechtsbitte vorangehen bei Busse in Höhe der Strafe des säumigen Richters

Among the Franks and Burgundians too, according to Cohn, a complaint of refusal of justice must be preceded by repeated requests for justice, on pain of a compensation equal to the penalty of the negligent judge

The reference, according to Liebermann, is not to a person who had a court of his own, but to one who was influential enough to shield his men from the operation of the law. He points out also that in case of appeal there is no mention here of an appeal to a county court such as we find in later times (cf. II Can. cap. 18).
Three times, according to later laws (cf. II Can. cap. 19).
